unmapped_findings: The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, calculated from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine equation (Eqs. 1-2) as an average over the whole experimental range (900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1), is 669.844 kJ mol^-1; the fitted slopes are k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690, and the stress level factor α = 0.00599.
Peak stress of this Fe-Mn-Al-C steel at 1100 °C and 10 s^-1 is above the 225 MPa level (Fig. 3(b)); the lnZ value for this condition is 60.98 (Table 1).

The dynamic recrystallization state diagram (Fig. 7) divides behaviour into area A (work hardening), area B (partial DRX) and area C (complete DRX) as functions of lnZ and strain; with increasing Z (increasing strain rate or decreasing T), the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs of DRX both increase.

From combining microstructure observation and DRX average grain size, the paper concludes that fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the ranges 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1; the present sample (1100 °C, 10 s^-1) falls in the latter range.
The DRX average grain size prediction model established with DEFORM-3D and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm is drex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338, with R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%.
